rationale: Both reviews are unusually thorough, cross-verifying nearly all the doc's technical claims (NPU/XPU/MUSA scope, prefix-cache incompatibility, full-payload-branch unreachability, guard table) against the code and correctly finding the diff already addresses most GT concerns. X edges ahead on recall by directly re-interrogating the single most substantive GT concern (connector-output ownership/snapshotting) and surfacing a plausible residual gap in the 'sole consumer' claim, plus a well-reasoned image-path/GitHub-rendering issue with a concrete suggested fix; its findings are also organized with clearer severity triage and actionable diffs. Y's findings (Thinker-only pipeline edge case, cross-doc optimization-stack inconsistency) are valuable and precisely evidenced but map less directly onto GT's specific concerns, and its validated-claims table appears to contradict X's connector-consumer finding, introducing some uncertainty. Neither surfaces the docs-build dependency-conflict issue from GT, and neither has a LATENT GAP CHECK section.
